the annual C emission:burial ratio is ten times larger for boreal than arctic lakes.
lakes in warmer boreals emit more and store less C than lakes at high latitudes and that this is important for the C cycle and climate feedbacks at high latitudes.
the ratio between annual C emission and burial rates is ten times higher in lakes of the boreal zone compared to lakes in the subarctic – Arctic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of boreal and arctictundra lakes as a source or sink of carbon in a warming climate.
the role of lakes in the global carbon cycle and how the balance between C burial and C emission is affected by climate and other drivers.
understanding the role of lakes in the global carbon cycle, and how lakes may respond to environmental change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C cycle of lakes at high latitudes is more complex than the terrestrial C cycle and that the C sink – source functions are not necessarily the same.
the net effect of climate warming on the high-latitude C sink is uncertain, and that it is important to include lake C cycling in future climate models.
the C balance in high latitude lakes is strongly controlled by climate, and that the C emission:burial ratio is a useful tool in assessing the role of lakes in the global C cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lakes in the arctic and subarctic regions are a major sink for carbon and that lakes in the boreal regions are a major source of carbon to the atmosphere.
the boreal lakes are more active in C cycling than arctic lakes.
the boreal biome is more active in terms of C emissions than the arctic biome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C balance in high latitude lakes is not only a function of lake size, but also a function of the climate zone in which the lake is located.
lake C cycling should be considered as an important component in global C cycle models, especially at high latitudes, as lakes play a key role in determining the C balance at high latitudes.
lakes in the boreal biome play a more important role in the continental C balance compared to arctic and subarctic lakes.
